note: Small access on the upper Gasconade River east of Hartville, at the end of a short gravel lane off Highway 38. The single primitive camping spot is the gravel turnaround lot at the lane's end, about 40 m from the river through bottomland woods. A path leads to a gravel bar and canoe launch. There's a picnic area, but no other facilities, and spot length is not published. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Designated Camping Sites' - one GIS camping point at the gravel lot at the end of the access lane off Hwy 38; free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit. Not waterfront kept (~40 m to the river through woods). Pin fine. Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: area page lists 'Camping: Designated Camping Sites' ('This conservation area offers access to the Gasconade River. There is a picnic area, gravel canoe launch...'). The 05/09 map predates the camping designation (no camping symbol), showing the gravel lane from Hwy 38 to a parking lot by the boat/canoe launch; GIS layer 27 point 1055 sits on that lot (layer 26 lot 2133, 14 m). On imagery the lot is a ~20 x 20 m gravel pad at the end of a ~400 m gravel lane - a 23-ft rig fits and can turn. No ford, 4WD note or posted limit.

WATERFRONT (stored not waterfront, kept): from the lot, the Gasconade channel (~30-40 m wide) is ~35-40 m west, measured on the 0.22 m/px leaf-off frame. Dense bottomland trees fill the strip between, so there's no open sightline. The gravel bar and canoe launch ~50-60 m NW are reached on foot.
